about: Mutations of the native side of the in-app updater, run by run-mutations.mjs: one exact replacement at a time in a throw-away copy; the native tests (or, for run "gate", CHATMCP-HUB/tests/verify-update-apply.mjs) must notice each. See docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

mutations.what: an address of any length is looked at

mutations.name: link-controls-allowed

mutations.name: link-non-ascii-allowed

mutations.name: link-single-slash

mutations.name: keys-field-range
mutations.what: coordinates beyond the field are taken
mutations.equivalent: A key with a coordinate beyond the field cannot be made with a private key we can sign with (the coordinate would have to be below 2^224 to add the prime without overflowing 256 bits), so no vector can carry a signature that verifies under it; the Hub refuses it too, by its canonical re-export.

mutations.name: sig-kid-line-break
mutations.what: the id of the key may end with a line break
mutations.equivalent: The key id is compared exactly with the ids of the keys in the list right after, so an id with a line break at the end finds none and is refused as unknown_kid.

mutations.name: sig-kid-capitals
mutations.what: the id of the key may be written in capitals
mutations.equivalent: The key id is compared exactly with the ids of the keys in the list right after (lower case, from the digest), so an id in capitals finds none and is refused as unknown_kid.

mutations.name: sig-length-unchecked
mutations.what: a signature of another length is tried
mutations.equivalent: VerifyData returns false for a signature of another length, so the file is refused as a mismatch instead of sig_length: the outcome is the same, only the reason differs.

mutations.name: sig-missing-field
mutations.what: a signature file without sig is read as an empty signature
mutations.equivalent: A missing or malformed sig is replaced by 64 zero bytes, which no key verifies, so the file is refused as a mismatch instead of sig_encoding: same outcome, another reason.

mutations.name: b64-not-canonical
mutations.what: base64 with spare bits is taken

mutations.name: b64-length-multiple
mutations.what: base64 whose length is not a multiple of 4 is tried
mutations.equivalent: Convert.FromBase64String throws a FormatException for a text whose length is not a multiple of 4, and the catch below answers null.

mutations.name: b64-alphabet
mutations.what: characters outside the base64 alphabet are tried
mutations.equivalent: A character outside the alphabet either makes Convert.FromBase64String throw (answered null) or is skipped as white space, and then the round trip (Convert.ToBase64String must give the text back) fails.

mutations.name: b64-size
mutations.what: base64 of any size is decoded
mutations.equivalent: Whatever the size, the callers refuse what is not 64 bytes (a signature) or 91 bytes (a key) right after, and the files that carry the text are cut at 4 KiB (signature) or come from the build (key list).

mutations.name: b64-line-break
mutations.what: base64 may end with a line break
mutations.equivalent: A line break at the end makes the text one character longer than a multiple of 4 or leaves a quantum short, so Convert.FromBase64String throws or the round trip fails, whichever way the pattern ends.
